comment: THE RULES OF SPEC SECTION 3.4, ONE ROW EACH, AS DATA. The runner is tests/lint-pairs.mjs and
reads nothing but this file and the fixtures beside it, so adding a rule is a row and two
files rather than a patch to a test.
`implemented` says whether the PINNED engine has the rule today, and it is not taken on
trust: the runner asserts that a rule marked false is silent on its own failing fixture, so a
rule that lands in the engine turns this file red rather than sitting here stale. That is the
recorded trap - an excuse list keyed by a name goes quiet when its subject changes - made
`expect` is a regular expression over one finding's text, and `severity` says which of the
linter's three lists it must appear in: errors, warnings, or the awaiting class board 505
added, which is a state rather than a fault and is counted apart for that reason. The twin
must produce nothing at all, in any of the three.
A ROW NAMING A LIST THE PINNED ENGINE DOES NOT RETURN FAILS LOUDLY rather than quietly: the
runner reads a missing list as empty and reports the failing fixture uncaught. That is the
wanted direction. missing-second-language reads `awaiting` since the pin moved to 4c377cb;
on an engine before board 505, which called every such card an error, this row is wrong and
this file says so on the first run.

rules.expect: ^card c-tosan: the id is claimed twice$
same title as card 1 in this category, so at the desk the two are hard to tell apart; one needs a title of its own, or the two can become one card$
^card c-tosan: requests names t-nowhere, which is no tag$
^card c-farlil: shelf t-nowhere names no tag$
